name: Todd Snyder
why: American menswear that names its Italian suppliers — the specific mill is printed on every product page — and a full own-label shoe program beside a curated wall of Alden, Paraboot, and Rubinacci.
origin: Todd Snyder, NYC, 2011 — ex-J.Crew menswear head with a Savile Row apprenticeship behind him.
opview: Positions itself as new American classics with the mills named.

onething.n: Works, but why is this THE ITEM

notes.ital: All the fabrics are Italian and the tailoring is made in Italy and Portugal — Tollegno cloth named on the product pages, a Pitti Uomo runway show, and Armani cited as the formative influence. Snyder learned to tailor in Des Moines and went to Italy for the cloth. Raised from 3 on 2026-08-09: the rubric says passport is not required, and this is an American brand with Italian mills, Italian make and Italian design language.
notes.golf: TS x FootJoy Premiere Series — a real golf-shoe line with the game's premier maker
notes.cotton: 54% of the clothing range, and 227 of those styles are 100% cotton — oxfords, selvedge denim, chinos, tees. Read across all 1,296 clothing products
notes.tech: almost none: 3% of the range is synthetic, spandex appears in 12% of styles at 1–3% for comfort rather than performance, and there is no house-named or licensed technology anywhere. Water resistance is claimed on eight styles
notes.craft: its fabric claim is provenance rather than technology. 321 styles state where the cloth comes from — Italy 195, Portugal 67, Japan 22 — concentrated in tailoring, with 33 of 39 sport coats Italian. Named mills are all third parties: Thomas Mason, Vitale Barberis Canonico, Baird McNutt, Albini, Kuroki

cities: ~15 stores — NYC, Boston, Chicago, DC & more · Nordstrom
